jobs.title: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE · The copier
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: Why the issue never ran: the library's copier at 7 AM with the Halloween pages face down on the glass, and the copier producing, instead of the pages, a single sheet — black, edge to edge, with a small white rectangle in the middle the size of a card. Wood keeps the black sheet. The pages go in Box 1. The card-sized white: reserved. Panel 1: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a teenage boy lifting the lid of a library photocopier with pages face down on the glass in early light (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a photocopier's output tray holding a single sheet printed solid black with a small white rectangle at its center. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a teenage boy holding a black sheet up to a window with a woman's cardigan sleeve at the frame's edge (in this panel: WOOD). Librarian says "It does that sometimes.". Panel 4: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a teenage boy placing comic pages into a cardboard box and a single black sheet into a folder (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
